findings.title: docs/delivery/agents.md (Process sandbox, D-030) still says 'the PID and IPC namespaces are private'. The code, the raw sandbox.json evidence and threat-model residual 8 all show the host PID namespace is shared. This is the same misstatement F-DG0-151 fixed in the agent_sandbox.py docstring, left in the agent-mechanism document
findings.reproduction: Candidate 21efe44b (450c756). `grep -n PID docs/delivery/agents.md` -> line 114: '- **Process:** only `CAP_SETFCAP` is kept, `no_new_privs` is set, and the PID and IPC namespaces are private.' Compare: (1) tools/agents/agent_sandbox.py bwrap_args passes `--unshare-ipc` and `--bind /proc /proc`; `grep -c unshare-pid tools/agents/agent_sandbox.py` = 0; the corrected module docstring (D-032) says it 'does NOT create a PID namespace'. (2) Raw evidence: sandbox.json of all three round-17 review runs (docs/delivery/runs/DG0/*R17*/sandbox.json) records `unshare: ["ipc"]`, `procfs: "host-bind"`. (3) docs/delivery/threat-model.md residual 8: 'The process sandbox shares the host PID namespace (D-030)'. The assignment asks QA to check that agents.md claims match the raw evidence (step 4). This sentence doesn't.
findings.expected: agents.md describes the process sandbox as the code and evidence do: host PID namespace shared (threat-model residual 8, with the reason: nested bwrap needs the host procfs), own IPC namespace (--unshare-ipc, D-031), host procfs bound read-write (residual 7). Suggested wording: '...`no_new_privs` is set, the IPC namespace is private, and the host PID namespace and procfs are shared (so a reviewer's nested bubblewrap works; threat-model residuals 7 and 8).'
findings.actual: A documentation-only overstatement of confinement in one summary sentence. The authoritative threat model and the code comment/docstring are correct, and the validator checks the real sandbox.json (`unshare` includes ipc, procfs host-bind), so no control or gate result depends on the wrong sentence. Low and non-mandatory. I'd accept it as an observation for DG0 if it's corrected in the next candidate (a one-line edit to a candidate file, owned by delivery-orchestrator).

history.note: Raised in the DG0 round-18 QA review of candidate 21efe44b (450c756). Low, documentation only; I'd accept it as an observation.
